A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Nautilus and provide readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably despite changes in formatting and appendix organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original mesh-generation experiments, tokenization measurements, reconstruction scores, a user study, and quantitative and qualitative ablations.

after.justification: v5 retains these empirical results and adds an original analysis of topological defects in the generated meshes.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same shell traversal, coordinate compression, dual-stream conditioning, autoregressive training objective, and image-conditioning procedure. Newly disclosed decoder dimensions do not establish an architecture change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 311K-mesh training collection and point-cloud and image-conditioned generation tasks. The added topology analysis reuses the existing 500 test outputs. The 7,000-face discussion is a projection, not an evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: The tokenization comparisons retain AMT and EdgeRunner; generation comparisons retain MeshAnything and MeshAnythingV2. The new topology table uses those same generation comparators. The expanded EdgeRunner discussion adds no evaluated baseline or direct point-cloud generation comparison.

E3.justification: v5 Appendix B.2 adds a protocol for evaluating existing outputs: boundary-edge detection of holes, PyMeshLab detection of intersecting faces, manual inspection of missing parts, and classification as manifold when all three defects are absent. Training settings, reconstruction evaluation, and user-study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 adds a focused defect analysis across the existing 500 generated meshes, quantifying structural failures previously illustrated qualitatively. The component ablations, compression-controlled AMT comparison, attention-map analysis, and sequence-length discussion are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The user-study sample information and attention-map averaging are unchanged. The new defect percentages are additional outcome metrics, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v5 Table 3 adds topology outcomes: manifold rates are 23.8%, 29.0%, and 83.6% for MeshAnything, MeshAnythingV2, and Nautilus; corresponding hole rates are 45.0%, 40.6%, and 4.2%. Intersection and missing-part rates are also new. Tables 1–2 and the quantitative ablation values remain unchanged. Figure 6 drops one comparative example.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and the mathematical content of Algorithm 1 are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive formal assumption is added. The new topology classifications are operational evaluation criteria, while the scaling discussion extrapolates from existing compression measurements.

C1.justification: The three central contributions remain locality-preserving tokenization, dual-stream conditioning, and scalable generation with detailed topology. The quarter-length representation and up-to-5,000-face generation claims persist. The new appendix evidence supports these retained contributions.

C2.justification: v5 Appendix F explicitly acknowledges that fully manifold output is not guaranteed and that intersecting-face reduction is weaker than hole reduction. Appendix C.1 adds interpretations of resource efficiency and projected scaling relative to EdgeRunner, while explaining the missing normals that obstruct direct point-cloud comparison.

D1.justification: v5 newly specifies the decoder's 1024 hidden dimensions and L40 GPU memory of 48GB, and identifies PyMeshLab and manual inspection for the topology audit. v1's promised project-page URL is removed. These are documentation and access-information changes, not evidence of retraining or changed resource availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the new Appendix C.1 substantially expand positioning against EdgeRunner, distinguishing tokenization, conditioning, training resources, and face-count scalability. The earlier 1,600-face characterization is qualified. References including BSP-Net, SpiralNet++, MeshCNN, and Edgebreaker are added, while the earlier image-conditioning citation to Bai et al. 2023 is removed.

P1.justification: The main argument and section sequence remain largely intact, with shortened prose and captions, a condensed conclusion, and added acknowledgments. The supplement gains a roadmap and reorganizes existing analyses, training statistics, and user-study details into separate sections.

P2.justification: v5 substantially changes the document template, typography, author layout, and caption placement. Tables 1–2 become vertically stacked, Figures 9–10 move into the supplement, and Figure 6 removes a row and replaces several source-mesh displays with point-cloud views. A topology-results table is added; most existing visual evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: The added topology audit directly strengthens evidence for structural fidelity, and Appendix F makes the limitations more explicit and precise. These are useful improvements within the existing evaluation coverage. The EdgeRunner resource comparisons and 7,000-face projection remain less conclusive than matched experiments, and removing the promised project-page pointer modestly reduces access information.
